thread:
Nina: heads-up: int3 bring-up perf looks promising but we see multilingual deid failures concentrated in CJK and Arabic scripts on long context jobs. Opening thread to coordinate dataset curation + tokenizer parity checks.

Ravi: Can you summarise failure modes? tokenization mismatch, wrong redaction, or hallucination?

Nina: Mostly redaction misses and weird chunk splits. Example: baseline masks a name as [REDACTED], int3 emits partial characters or inserts spaces inside CJK tokens. Also Arabic diacritics get normalized differently leading to mismatch with fingerprinting.

Nina: ```
# redacted example (sanitized)
prompt: "Please redact names and phone numbers from this multilingual transcript."
baseline: "[REDACTED] 电话: [REDACTED]"
int3: "李 小: 电话: 123-XXX-XXXX"  # split across tokens -> failed redact
```

Sam: That split-token behavior smells like tokenizer normalization differences + a quantized embedding lookup rounding bug. We should run tokenizer parity tests between baseline and int3 builds. @Eun can you run tokenization diffs?

Eun: On it. I'll run parallel tokenization on a 5k sample (mix of zh, ja, ko, ar, he, ru). ETA 6h. Will post diff report.

Marta: For dataset ops: we should dedupe after canonical normalization to avoid missing duplicates because of diacritics/spaces. Proposing pipeline change: normalize -> unicode_nfc -> remove_zero_width -> strip_zwj -> lower/upper as appropriate -> then fingerprint.

Sam: Agreed. Current dedupe runs before normalization which explains low recall on duplicate detection for multilingual. Any small code change to canonicalize pre-fingerprint will help match existing golden items.

LabelOpsBot: Current labeling backlog: pending=98, active=30. Suggested micro-golden size: 1500 (lang-balanced) to triage int3 regressions. ETA w/current pool: 48h.

Nina: Proposed sampling plan: 1500 items split by language: zh=400, ja=200, ko=150, ar=300, he=100, ru=150, other=200. Include heavy-context (>512 tokens) subset = 35% of sample. Also include 200 synthetic transliterations and spacing-variant paraphrases.

Marta: I'll generate the synthetic paraphrases using the translit job and add a normalization flag in metadata: `needs_norm_review`. Labelers should mark whether failure is tokenization/normalization vs model hallucination.

Ravi: Can we add a label task checkbox: [ ] normalization_issue  [ ] redact_missed  [ ] hallucination  [ ] truncation? That'll let us compute per-failure-type rates quickly.

LabelOpsBot: Added checkboxes to label schema: normalization_issue, redact_missed, hallucination, truncation. Project created: `int3-multilang-deid-microgolden`. SLA=36h.

Sam: For evaluation, I'll add per-lang precision/recall, and an extra metric: normalization-adjusted recall where we apply our canonicalizer post-hoc to judge true duplicate redaction. If that gap is large, it points at dedupe/tokenizer mismatch rather than model semantics.

Eun: Tokenizer diff plan: run `tools/tokenizer_diff.py --model int3 --baseline quant4b --langs zh,ja,ko,ar,he,ru --sample 5000 --out diffs/int3_token_diffs.json`. I'll include examples where token boundaries moved relative to baseline.

Nina: If tokenizer diffs show boundary shifts for >2% of tokens in long contexts, we should hold roll and route deid traffic to quant4b until we patch. DeployBot, can we create a fallback route?

DeployBot: Canary routing plan created: route deid and RAG requests with lang in [zh,ja,ko,ar,he,ru] AND ctx_tokens>512 -> quant4b-fallback. Will hold for manual flip once metrics clear.

Ravi: Ops/engineering action items:
- Eun: run tokenizer diffs and post report (6h)
- Marta: build 1.5k lang-balanced sample + synthetic paraphrases, run canonicalizer then fingerprint dedupe (12h)
- LabelOps: spin label job and enforce checkbox schema (now)
- Sam: create eval dashboard with normalization-adjusted metrics (12h)
- Nina: coordinate with runtime if fallback routing needed (standby)

Marta: note: when generating synthetic transliterations, tag source script and transliteration method (icu/heuristic). We'll need that metadata in eval so we can see if particular translit methods expose fragility.

Eun: quick note from tokenizer run (partial): initial pass shows CJK token boundary diffs concentrated at punctuation+emoji boundaries. Sending raw diffs in 2h.

Sam: timeline: aim to have micro-golden labeled by Fri EOD, run canary on Sat, decision Sat evening. If we see tokenization-normalization gap >4% per-lang, plan to hold roll and issue hotfix.

Nina: thanks everyone. I'll drop sample CSV and normalization script link here once ready. If you see small edgecases (zero-width space, bidi markers), flag them in the label job comments.

Marta: pushing sample to /label-ops/int3-multilang now (link omitted).

LabelOpsBot: Project `int3-multilang-deid-microgolden` updated: tasks=1500, assigned_shifts=36, est_completion=44h with current pool.

Ravi: ping @Eun and @Marta for early diffs. We'll sync again after tokenizer report. :mag:

Eun: will post diffs and a short summary in ~2h.
